newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-HENMAN FIRST ON NEW COURT ONE AS KRAJICEK STARTS DEFENCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HENMAN FIRST ON NEW COURT ONE AS KRAJICEK STARTS DEFENCE.

text.p: Richard Krajicek starts the defence of his Wimbledon title against little-known German Marcello Craca in the opening match on centre court on Monday
Dutchman Krajicek, seeded fourth this year at the All England club, seems to have little to fear from the unseeded Craca.
The first match on court one features Britain Tim Henman, the 14th seed, against powerful Canadian Daniel Nestor.
Henman, who delighted his home fans by reaching the quarter-finals last year, will be cheered by 12,500 fans on Wimbledon's brand new show court which will be officially opened on Monday.
Henman and Nestor will be followed by German Michael Stich, the 1991 champion, and American former world number one Jim Courier.
Stich, making his final Wimbledon appearance as he has said he would retire at the end of the year, can expect a strong challenge from Courier, always a tough competitor.

Both French Open champions will be in action on the first day of the championships with Croat Iva Majoli, the fourth seed, playing Argentina's Mariana Diaz Oliva on court two and Brazilian Gustavo Kuerten facing American Justin Gimelstob on court three.
Kuerten, seeded 11th thanks to his sensational Paris win, promised to change his flashy, yellow and blue outfit for more traditional clothes.

One of the most exciting clashes of a first day, which could well be marred by rain, should be the one between seventh seeded Australian Mark Philippoussis and Briton Greg Rusedski, two of the hardest hitters on the men's circuit. They will play on centre court immediately after Krajicek and Craca.

Other matches to watch include second-seeded American Monica Seles, chasing the only grand slam title to elude her, against Australian Rachel McQuillan on court one and hard-hitting Croat Goran Ivanisevic against Romanian Dinu Pescariu on court two.
Ivanisevic, seeded second this year, has reached the Wimbledon final twice, in 1992 and 1994.
American teenager Venus Williams, seen by many as a likely candidate for the number one spot in the near future, makes her Wimbledon debut against Poland's Magdalena Grzybowska on court three.
